abort.unique_id_mismatch: This connection belongs to a different wallbox.
abort.service_migration_requires_serial: The wallbox needs a readable serial number to match the existing device during migration.
abort.invalid_service_discovery: The app reported invalid connection details.
abort.service_identity_changed: The discovered wallbox changed. Start setup again.
abort.service_discovery_updated: The existing integration now uses the discovered app connection.
abort.multiple_service_apps: Multiple Modbus apps were found. Select the matching discovered app under Devices & services.
abort.connection_settings_changed: Connection settings changed during authentication. The checked credentials were not saved. Review the current connection before trying again.
abort.reauth_not_supported: This connection does not use adapter TCP login. Use Change connection to update its settings.

error.cannot_connect: Could not open the serial port or the wallbox did not answer. Check the cabling (Modbus A is +, B is -), the port and the bus parameters.
error.invalid_response: The device answered but did not report a Modbus layout version. Check the device address and whether DIP 4 and DIP 5 on bank S1 are on.
error.not_found: No wallbox answered on this port. Check the wiring (Modbus A is +, B is -, GND connected) and that DIP 4 and DIP 5 on bank S1 are on, with the wallbox restarted afterwards.
error.cannot_connect_service: The app cannot be reached over the network. Check that it is running and accepting connections on port 8765.
error.service_discovery_requires_serial: The app has not read a serial number yet. Check its wallbox connection and try again.
error.service_auth_failed: The Modbus service rejected authentication. For a Supervisor app, confirm again to retrieve its current credentials. For a separately hosted service, enter its current access token.
error.service_not_ready: Authentication to the app succeeded, but wallbox data is not available yet. Check the app log and try again.
error.service_invalid_response: The app responds, but its data was not accepted. The Home Assistant log identifies the affected data section. Check the log and download diagnostics before restarting the app.
error.invalid_network_config: Enter a host name or IP address without a URL scheme, a TCP port from 1 to 65535 and the matching connection protocol.
error.cannot_connect_network: Could not reach the LAN adapter or the wallbox did not answer. Check the host, port, protocol and the serial settings configured on the adapter.
error.invalid_network_response: The adapter answered but no valid Modbus layout was reported. Check the wallbox address, adapter protocol and satellite configuration.
error.service_discovery_unavailable: The current credentials of this app could not be retrieved. Check the app and Supervisor, start or restart the app if needed, then confirm again.
error.service_version_mismatch: The Modbus service does not meet this integration’s API or minimum-version requirements. Use a compatible service version as described in the integration’s release notes. If both components need updating, update the app or standalone service first.
error.invalid_tcp_auth_password: Enter the existing adapter web password: 1–9 printable ASCII characters, without spaces.
error.invalid_gateway_config: Check the supported baud rate, frame and existing web password. TCP login requires a valid password.
error.gateway_unsupported: This adapter model, firmware or operating mode cannot be configured automatically. Configure the adapter manually and turn off “Set up LAN adapter”.
error.gateway_unreachable: The adapter settings could not be read. Check the address and local network access, or use manual configuration.
error.gateway_changed: The adapter settings changed since this preview. Start the connection setup again to read the current settings.
error.gateway_apply_failed: The adapter settings could not be applied and verified. Check the existing web password and adapter connection.
error.gateway_rollback_failed: The previous adapter settings could not be confirmed after a failed change. The old integration connection remains stopped. Check the adapter settings manually before reconnecting.
error.gateway_authentication_failed: The adapter rejected its existing web password. Check the password used for its web interface.

progress.searching: Searching the bus for a wallbox: up to {candidates} combinations, about {minutes} minutes plus connection checks. No registers are written. During reconfiguration, the existing connection and heartbeat are paused; the wallbox's configured fallback applies.

reconfigure.title: Change connection
reconfigure.description: Choose the new connection for this wallbox. For a connection managed by the Modbus app, change its USB or LAN settings in the app instead. Keep only one Modbus connection to the wallbox active.

search_result.description:
A wallbox answered after {attempts} attempts:

- Device address: **{device_id}**
- Bus: **{baudrate} baud, {frame}**
- Modbus layout: **{layout}**
- Serial number: **{serial_number}**

Submit to set the wallbox up with these values.
search_result.title: Wallbox found

user.title: Connect to your wallbox
user.description: Choose how Home Assistant reaches the wallbox. The optional Modbus app is recommended: it keeps the heartbeat running during a Home Assistant restart. A running Supervisor app is discovered automatically. Direct USB or LAN connections do not require the app.

data.search: If these values do not work

data_description.baudrate: Must match the wallbox setting. The factory default is 57600 baud.
data_description.device_id: Factory default is 50. Addresses from 10 to 50 can be set with the MENNEKES configuration tool.
data_description.frame: Data bits, parity and stop bits must match the wallbox. The factory default is 8N2.
data_description.port: Path of the USB RS-485 adapter. Prefer a /dev/serial/by-id path: /dev/ttyUSB0 can change between reboots.
data_description.search: The device address and the bus parameters can be changed with the MENNEKES configuration tool, so an inherited installation often uses something else. Searching sends read requests. Only use it on a bus without another Modbus master.

serial.description: The wallbox has to be configured as a Modbus satellite: DIP switches 4 and 5 on bank S1 on, then restart the wallbox. This integration is validated against register layout {validated_layout}.
serial.title: Mennekes Amtron RTU

server.title: Connect to the Modbus service
server.description: Supervisor apps connect automatically without entering a URL or token. This form is for a separately hosted service. When migrating from direct Modbus, disable the previous integration entry first to release the Modbus connection.

data_description.server_url: HTTP address of the independent Modbus service, normally on port 8765. Do not enter the Modbus LAN adapter address here.
data_description.server_token: Use the access token configured in the separately hosted service. The Supervisor app supplies its token automatically; you do not need this form for that app.

hassio_confirm.title: Connect the Modbus app
hassio_confirm.description: The Modbus app was discovered automatically. Its address and access token are supplied for you. Confirm the connection. An existing entry for this wallbox keeps its device and entity IDs. A disabled entry remains disabled until you enable it again.

network.title: Connect through a LAN adapter
network.description: Connect a supported RTU wallbox through an Ethernet-to-RS-485 adapter. Select transparent RTU over TCP or a gateway that translates Modbus TCP to RTU. Configure baud rate and frame on the adapter. Use a trusted private network and exclusive access to the bus. Validated register layout: {validated_layout}.

data.host: Adapter IP address or host name

data_description.connection_type: Match the adapter mode: transparent RTU over TCP or translating Modbus TCP to RTU.
data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the LAN adapter, without http:// or any URL path.
data_description.tcp_port: TCP port configured on the adapter; default 502. This is not the independent service HTTP port 8765.
data_description.device_id: Wallbox address behind the adapter; factory default 50, supported range 10–50.
data_description.tcp_authentication: Use the login already enabled on the adapter. This switch alone does not enable it on the adapter; select “Set up LAN adapter” to change that setting. Login does not encrypt the traffic. Firmware 1.523 allows bypassing it; use a protected local network.
data_description.configure_gateway: Detect a compatible adapter, then choose and apply its TCP login, serial speed, data format, connection protocol and TCP port. The next page lets you review the settings before saving.

network_reconfigure.title: Connect through a LAN adapter
network_reconfigure.description: Connect a supported RTU wallbox through an Ethernet-to-RS-485 adapter. Select transparent RTU over TCP or a gateway that translates Modbus TCP to RTU. Configure baud rate and frame on the adapter. Use a trusted private network and exclusive access to the bus. Validated register layout: {validated_layout}.

data.host: Adapter IP address or host name

data_description.connection_type: Match the adapter mode: transparent RTU over TCP or translating Modbus TCP to RTU.
data_description.host: Host name or IP address of the LAN adapter, without http:// or any URL path.
data_description.tcp_port: TCP port configured on the adapter; default 502. This is not the independent service HTTP port 8765.
data_description.device_id: Wallbox address behind the adapter; factory default 50, supported range 10–50.
data_description.tcp_authentication: Use the login already enabled on the adapter. This switch alone does not enable it on the adapter; select “Set up LAN adapter” to change that setting. Login does not encrypt the traffic. Firmware 1.523 allows bypassing it; use a protected local network.
data_description.configure_gateway: Detect a compatible adapter, then choose and apply its TCP login, serial speed, data format, connection protocol and TCP port. The next page lets you review the settings before saving.

reauth_confirm.title: Renew service access
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the current access token for your separately hosted Modbus service. The service URL and existing wallbox entry are kept.

reauth_app.title: Renew app access
reauth_app.description: Confirm to retrieve the current credentials of this Modbus app from Supervisor. The app must be running. You do not need to enter a token.

network_auth.title: Log in to the LAN adapter
network_auth.description: Enter the existing web password of your compatible adapter. This checks the connection without changing the adapter’s settings or password. Use 1–9 printable ASCII characters without spaces. Login does not encrypt the traffic. Firmware 1.523 allows bypassing it; use a protected local network.

data_description.tcp_auth_password: The password you use to open the adapter’s own web interface, not a Home Assistant or app access token. TCP login accepts 1–9 printable ASCII characters without spaces.

network_adapter.title: Set up LAN adapter
network_adapter.description:
Recognized: **{model}**, firmware **{firmware}**. Current serial settings: **{baudrate} baud, {frame}**, TCP port **{tcp_port}**.

Submitting applies the connection protocol and TCP port chosen on the previous page together with the settings below. It then checks the wallbox identity. If validation fails, the previous adapter settings are restored where reachable. Your existing web password is not changed. This also selects passive TCP-server operation and disables the adapter’s own Modbus polling/cache, flow control, connection preambles, replay of buffered serial data, automatic parameter uploads and data-triggered restarts.

data.tcp_authentication: Enable TCP login on the adapter

data_description.tcp_authentication: Saving enables or disables login on the adapter and configures this integration to match. Login uses the existing adapter web password; it does not create or change that password. Login does not encrypt the traffic. Firmware 1.523 allows bypassing it; use a protected local network.
data_description.tcp_auth_password: Enter the current adapter web password, if set. TCP login requires a password with 1–9 printable ASCII characters without spaces. The password is saved only when TCP login is enabled.
data_description.baudrate: Must match the wallbox setting. The factory default is 57600 baud.
data_description.frame: Data bits, parity and stop bits must match the wallbox. The factory default is 8N2.

network_reauth.title: Log in to the LAN adapter
network_reauth.description: Enter the existing web password of your compatible adapter. This checks the connection without changing the adapter’s settings or password. Use 1–9 printable ASCII characters without spaces. Login does not encrypt the traffic. Firmware 1.523 allows bypassing it; use a protected local network.

data_description.tcp_auth_password: The password you use to open the adapter’s own web interface, not a Home Assistant or app access token. TCP login accepts 1–9 printable ASCII characters without spaces.

state.early_at_minimum: May finish early at minimum current

state.departure_plan: Departure plan is preparing the current

release_off_on_unplug.name: Switch off charging release when unplugged

state.phase_timeout: Vehicle did not become ready in time
state.phase_unconfirmed: Phase selection could not be confirmed

charging_current_invalid.message: {value} A is not a valid charging-current limit. The wallbox accepts 0 A (no limit) or at least {minimum} A; anything in between makes it signal 0 A to the vehicle.

charging_current_zero.message: 0 A does not stop charging on this wallbox: it removes the limit and the wallbox signals its maximum current. Use the charging-pause switch to pause, or call the "Set charging current" action with "allow unlimited" if you really want no limit.

entry_not_loaded.message: The wallbox entry for device {device} is not loaded.

no_wallbox_target.message: The action needs at least one MENNEKES AMTRON device as its target.

phase_switch_unsupported.message: This wallbox cannot switch between one and three phases. Dynamic phase switching needs an 11 kW device that reports phase option 2.

read_only_mode.message: This wallbox is in read-only mode. For a service connection, disable Read-only in the app, save and restart the app. For a direct USB or LAN connection, select Modbus master in the integration options.

restart_requires_idle.message: The wallbox may only be restarted while it is idle. Unplug the vehicle first.

unknown_device.message: Device {device} is not known to Home Assistant.

write_rate_limited.message: Wait {seconds} s before writing this change again.

phase_state_unknown.message: The current charging state could not be confirmed. No phases were switched. Check the connection and try again.

phase_pause_timeout.message: The vehicle did not confirm the charging pause in time. No phase-change command was sent. Check the charging state before trying again.

phase_pause_state_unknown.message: The charging pause could not be confirmed. No phase-change command was sent. Check the connection and charging state before trying again.

restart_state_unknown.message: The current charging state could not be confirmed. No restart was requested. Check the connection and try again.

recovery_not_applicable.message: The wallbox reports an error other than heartbeat error 200. No recovery commands were sent.

recovery_state_unknown.message: The current error or charging-current state could not be confirmed. No recovery commands were sent.

service_unavailable.message: The Modbus service is unavailable or could not confirm the command. Check the current state before repeating it.

service_auth_failed.message: The Modbus service rejected authentication. Renew its access under Settings > Devices & services.

device_identity_changed.message: The connection reports a different wallbox or cannot confirm its configured identity. Check the device address and service or adapter configuration. Control stays unavailable until the configured wallbox can be confirmed again.

service_version_mismatch.message: The Modbus service does not meet this integration’s API or minimum-version requirements. Use a compatible service version as described in the integration’s release notes. If both components need updating, update the app or standalone service first.

control_state_unknown.message: The current wallbox state could not be confirmed. No charging release, unlock or phase-change command was sent. Check the connection and try again.

energy_goal_invalid.message: Enter 0 to disable the energy target, or 0.1–1000 kWh in 0.1 kWh steps.

energy_goal_unavailable.message: An energy target needs a supported total-energy meter and a fresh valid reading. Check the connection and try again.

energy_goal_stop_active.message: A charging target requires a pause. Check its status. After reaching a target or a meter reset, set a new target or disable it with 0 before resuming. Changing a target does not start charging.

energy_goal_state_invalid.message: The saved energy target could not be restored. Check the logs before allowing charging again.

energy_goal_not_supported.message: This Modbus service does not support energy targets. Update the app or standalone service first.

cancel_pending_not_supported.message: This Modbus service cannot cancel pending changes. Update the app or standalone service first.

soc_goal_invalid.message: Enter a target from 0 to 100%, no higher than the vehicle charge limit. 0 disables the percentage target.

soc_goal_unavailable.message: The vehicle charge target cannot be changed right now. Check the configured vehicle sources and try again.

soc_goal_limit_unavailable.message: The selected vehicle charge limit has not provided a valid value yet. Wait for it to become available before setting a percentage target. 0 remains available to disable the target.

soc_goal_source_changed.message: The vehicle sources have changed. Reload the integration before changing its percentage target.

soc_goal_app_update_required.message: Update the Mennekes Modbus service app before changing the vehicle percentage target. Other wallbox functions remain available.

soc_goal_not_supported.message: The Modbus service does not support vehicle percentage targets. Update the app to use this optional feature.

soc_goal_state_invalid.message: The saved vehicle charge target could not be restored. Check the logs before allowing charging again.

loss_source_invalid.message: Select a supported charging loss source and configure its matching vehicle or sensor.

loss_unavailable.message: No complete charging session is available to match. The wallbox connection must remain available from plugging in until unplugging.

loss_energy_invalid.message: The vehicle energy cannot be matched. Select valid battery energy for this charge, greater than zero and no higher than the wallbox energy. You may correct the latest assignment.

loss_storage_unavailable.message: The charging loss could not be saved. Check storage availability and try again.

timed_goal_state_invalid.message: The saved departure time could not be restored. Check the stored plan before charging again.

timed_goal_unavailable.message: Queued departure commands could not be checked. The integration will retry when the connection is available.

timed_vehicle_unavailable.message: No usable upcoming departure was found for the selected vehicle. Check its integration, timer sensors and settings.

gateway_authentication_failed.message: The adapter rejected its existing web password. Check the password used for its web interface.

vehicle_profile_invalid.message: Select an existing, unambiguous vehicle profile.

vehicle_selection_changed.message: The vehicle selection changed during setup. Setup will retry with the current selection.

plug_charge_unavailable.message: Virtual Plug & Charge is currently unavailable. Check the wallbox or Modbus app connection and try again.

plug_charge_blocked.message: Automatic charging is currently blocked. Check vehicle permission, manual pause and charging targets.

plug_charge_session_changed.message: The vehicle connection or permission settings changed. Charging permission was not applied; wait for the current session to be recognized again.

plug_charge_authorization_expired.message: The vehicle authorization has expired or is no longer valid. Wait for fresh matching vehicle data before trying again.

plug_charge_not_supported.message: The connected Modbus app or service does not support Virtual Plug & Charge. Update it to a compatible version before enabling this feature.

heartbeat_unavailable.title: Wallbox heartbeat is not confirmed
heartbeat_unavailable.description: The controller has not received confirmation of the wallbox heartbeat for at least one minute. Check power to the wallbox and adapter, the USB or LAN connection, and the RS485 wiring. In app mode, also check the app log. This notice clears automatically when the heartbeat is confirmed again.

service_unavailable.title: Connection to the Modbus app is unavailable
service_unavailable.description: For at least one minute, Home Assistant could not verify its connection to the Modbus app. The app may continue its heartbeat independently. Check that the app is running and its network connection is working. This notice clears automatically when the connection returns.

ems_fallback_not_configured.description: Register 0x030E is 0, so the wallbox keeps charging with the last values it received when the active Modbus master stops sending a heartbeat. Configure a fallback behaviour or a fallback current with the MENNEKES configuration tool to get a defined state during an outage.
ems_fallback_not_configured.title: No energy-manager fallback configured

confirm.description: The wallbox reports error 200 after a missing heartbeat. When writes are enabled, automatic recovery reasserts the existing controls when heartbeat delivery resumes, including while charging is paused. Confirm to retry manually. A deliberate pause, device lock, disabled charging release and current setting are preserved. This does not resume charging. A resolved issue closes without sending commands.
confirm.title: Wallbox lost the energy-manager heartbeat

error.entry_unavailable: The integration is not loaded. Restore its connection before retrying.
error.different_error: The wallbox reports a different error. Heartbeat recovery does not reset that error.
error.read_only: Disable Read-only in the app, save and restart the app before requesting recovery. For a direct USB or LAN connection, enable Modbus master mode in the integration options instead.
error.write_rate_limited: A recent command is still inside its minimum write interval. Wait briefly and try again.
error.recovery_failed: The recovery could not be confirmed. Check the connection and retry.
error.still_active: The recovery commands were sent, but the wallbox still reports an error. Wait for its status to update; check the connection if the error persists.

unsupported_modbus_layout.description: The wallbox reports register layout {layout}; this integration is validated against {validated_layout}. Entities for registers your firmware does not have are not created. A firmware update through the MENNEKES configuration tool enables them.
unsupported_modbus_layout.title: Wallbox uses an older Modbus register layout

write_rejected.description: A write was not confirmed. Check the USB or LAN connection and the wallbox satellite configuration. This issue clears after the affected command succeeds. Historical failures remain in the diagnostic counter.
write_rejected.title: Wallbox refused a write

init.title: Settings
init.description: Start with Wallbox. Vehicle data, departure planning, cost estimates and charging losses are optional. Each section is saved separately on its final form; only settings for the features you choose are shown.

wallbox.title: Wallbox
wallbox.description: Set the maximum current Home Assistant may request and how often it reads status. With the Modbus app, write permission and bus timing belong in the app’s Configuration tab. USB/LAN connection changes belong in Reconfigure for direct connections, or in the app for app connections.

wallbox_basic.title: Current limit and polling

data_description.control_mode: Both modes send read requests and require exclusive bus access. Read only does not write registers. Modbus master additionally sends the heartbeat and enables control entities. Do not share this bus with another master.
data_description.current_limit: Upper limit for the charging-current control, in amperes per phase. This is not a percentage target or a pause command. The wallbox’s own limit and, when used, the app’s limit also apply.
data_description.scan_interval_seconds: How often charging status, errors and controls are read. The heartbeat runs independently.

wallbox_basic.description: The current cap limits requests from HA; the wallbox and service limits still apply. For app connections, the polling interval only affects HA’s service requests.

wallbox_advanced.title: Measurements and switching delays

data_description.measurement_interval_seconds: Power, voltage, current and session values: 30 seconds reduces database load. Status changes refresh immediately. Without a vehicle, at least 60 seconds. The status interval sets the shortest possible polling time.
data_description.state_change_interval_seconds: Minimum seconds between charging starts, pauses, release changes, locking or unlocking, and phase changes (default 300). Early commands are queued; the latest command replaces the previous one. The five-second current-write interval still applies. Set 0 to disable the longer interval.
data_description.phase_switch_grace_seconds: Extra seconds to wait after the vehicle confirms its charging pause, before switching phases (default 5, range 0–30). Set 0 to skip only this extra wait; confirmation of the pause is still required.

wallbox_advanced.description: The defaults balance quick status updates, fewer stored measurements and gentle switching. A queued command shows its remaining wait in Home Assistant. These intervals do not slow the independent heartbeat.

vehicle.title: Vehicle
vehicle.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Configure vehicle profiles and the optional percentage target. Select each car once, then choose independently whether to use its charge limit, capacity, departure timers or history.

To cancel only the current percentage target, set Vehicle charge target to 0. Stop using vehicle charge level removes this profile’s source assignments here, including the optional maximum, clears its percentage target and departure plan, and disables departure planning. The source entities in the vehicle integration remain unchanged, as do vehicle permission, the kWh target and charging state.

vehicle_soc.title: Configure charge level

data.use_vehicle_limit: Also use the vehicle’s charge limit

data_description.vehicle_soc_entity: Choose the vehicle sensor reporting its actual charge level in %. Missing data leaves charging unchanged until valid data returns. Changing the source clears the percentage target without resuming charging. To disable it, use the previous menu.
data_description.use_vehicle_limit: Enable this to select the vehicle’s own charge limit as an additional maximum. No setting is written to the vehicle.

vehicle_soc.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

This enables the optional percentage target using an existing charge-level sensor. Afterwards, set the desired percentage on the wallbox device page. Setting a target only limits charging; it does not cancel a manual pause.

vehicle_limit.title: Vehicle charge limit

data_description.vehicle_charge_limit_entity: Optional: additionally cap the percentage target using the vehicle’s charge-limit entity. Without this entity, targets up to 100% are available. A lower limit reduces an existing target; a higher limit does not raise it. The last valid limit remains in force if this entity is unavailable. No setting is written to the vehicle.

vehicle_limit.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Use the vehicle’s configured charging limit as an additional maximum for the Home Assistant percentage target. Select the desired limit reported by the car, not its current charge level.

departure.title: Next departure
departure.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Plan one next trip with a percentage target, usable battery capacity and departure time. Choose the actual time afterwards on the device page, or copy it from an optional source. This is not a daily schedule. Disabling planning clears the trip and queued plan commands; the percentage target remains.

departure_requires_vehicle.title: Charge level required
departure_requires_vehicle.description: Configure a vehicle charge-level source first, then return to departure planning.

departure_configure.title: Configure departure planning
departure_configure.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Manual date and time entry is always available. Enable only the additional sources you want; their settings appear next. An active plan can resume a manual pause to meet departure.

data_description.capacity_source: Use usable battery capacity: a fixed value, a kWh/Wh sensor, or the profile value when supported. The plan waits if its chosen capacity or charge level is unavailable.
data_description.use_calendar: Adds a button to copy the next matching calendar event. Each press chooses one trip; use the supplied blueprint if you want scheduled calendar imports.
data_description.use_departure_entity: Automatically adopts a new future date and time from the selected entity. Manual selection remains possible; a different future timestamp from this source can replace it.
data_description.use_vehicle_timer: Adds a button to copy one active departure/climate timer from the vehicle integration. It reads the reported timer; it does not switch on the car’s climate control.

departure_capacity_fixed.title: Usable battery capacity

data_description.timed_capacity_kwh: Enter the usable battery capacity, not the nominal capacity.

departure_capacity_fixed.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Enter the energy the battery can actually store for driving. This value is used to estimate the required charging time; changing it does not change the car’s own battery settings.

departure_capacity_entity.title: Battery capacity entity

data_description.timed_capacity_entity: Select a sensor that reports usable battery capacity in kWh or Wh.

departure_capacity_entity.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Choose a sensor for usable capacity, not remaining energy or charge percentage. Its unit must be kWh or Wh. Without a valid value, the plan waits for capacity instead of guessing.

departure_calendar.title: Departure calendar

data_description.timed_calendar_entity: Select a calendar and press Use next calendar event to copy one matching event into the departure time.
data_description.timed_calendar_title: Only events with this exact title are eligible. All-day events are ignored.

departure_calendar.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Choose a calendar and an exact event title, for example “Drive to work”. The event start becomes the departure time. The button searches the next 14 days; all-day events are ignored.

departure_entity.title: Departure time entity

data_description.timed_departure_entity: Select a dated timestamp sensor or an input_datetime with date and time. A time of day alone cannot identify the next trip.

departure_entity.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Choose a source containing both date and time. A valid new future timestamp is adopted automatically. Configure only one source for this purpose; manual entry and the calendar/vehicle buttons remain available.

departure_vehicle.title: Vehicle integration
departure_vehicle.description: Choose an installed integration with a supported adapter. Generic HA entities can be selected without an adapter. Only existing local vehicle data is read.

departure_vehicle_details.title: Vehicle departure timers

data_description.timed_vehicle_time_zone: Vehicle time zone, for example Europe/Berlin. Leave empty to use the Home Assistant time zone. BMW timer clocks contain no time zone.
data_description.timed_timer1_days: Choose the days configured for recurring climate timer 1 in the BMW. BavarianData does not expose these days. Leave empty to ignore this timer.
data_description.timed_timer2_days: Choose the days configured for recurring climate timer 2 in the BMW. Leave empty to ignore this timer.

departure_vehicle_details.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Use the departure button to copy one active timer from the selected vehicle. With a profile, the vehicle is already selected. For BavarianData, enable the timer action, hour and minute sensors; enter recurring weekdays here because the integration does not publish them.

costs.title: Electricity price source
costs.description: Choose a fixed electricity price or an existing price sensor. Disabled turns off cost estimates. Additional network-tariff steps appear when Home Assistant’s country is Germany.

data_description.charging_cost_source: Fixed price suits a constant contract price; a sensor can follow a dynamic tariff such as Tibber. This estimates charging costs only and does not choose the cheapest charging times.

cost_fixed.title: Fixed electricity price
cost_fixed.description: Enter the price per kWh including taxes. Negative prices are supported. With no network adjustment, this must be your final price including network charges. Standing charges and annual credits are excluded. The initial suggestion is 0.40 EUR/kWh; use your own contract price.

data_description.charging_price: Enter euros per kWh, including taxes: 0.40 means 40 cents/kWh. Use the energy price from your contract; any network-price adjustment is configured separately.

cost_sensor.title: Electricity price sensor
cost_sensor.description: Select a sensor with the current gross electricity price in EUR/kWh, ct/kWh or EUR/MWh (the € symbol is also supported). Negative prices are allowed. Without network adjustment, the price must include network charges. A report stays valid for 90 minutes; reporting the same value renews it. Missing or expired prices leave that energy unpriced. Standing charges and annual credits are excluded.

data_description.charging_price_entity: Choose the price for electricity consumed now, not a daily average, forecast list or export price. Its unit must identify EUR/kWh, ct/kWh or EUR/MWh.

cost_module2.title: Module 2: reduced network price

data.price_includes_network: Electricity price already includes the regular network price

data_description.price_includes_network: Enabled: subtract the regular network price before adding the selected network tariff. Disabled: the electricity source excludes network charges, so add the network tariff. Choose this carefully to avoid counting network charges twice.
data_description.regular_network: Regular gross network energy price from the operator’s price sheet, in EUR/kWh. Enter the unreduced amount; the integration calculates the Module 2 reduction.

cost_module2.description: Enter the gross regular network price. Module 2 applies 40% of this component, not 40% of the whole electricity price.

cost_module3_source.title: Module 3: tariff source
cost_module3_source.description: Manual entry does not send your location unless you later enable annual refresh. Import sends HA Home coordinates to VNBdigital and retrieves public tariffs from Par14a-Database. Review the operator, prices and time windows before saving. If no unique tariff is found, enter the values manually.

cost_module3_prices.title: Module 3: prices and time windows

data.price_includes_network: Electricity price already includes the regular network price
data.auto_tariff_refresh: Refresh Module 3 tariff automatically at the new year

data_description.price_includes_network: Enabled: subtract the regular network price before adding the selected network tariff. Disabled: the electricity source excludes network charges, so add the network tariff. Choose this carefully to avoid counting network charges twice.
data_description.auto_tariff_refresh: From 1 January, retrieves the new year’s tariff using HA Home coordinates and applies a valid unique result. Sends coordinates to VNBdigital again; retries daily if needed. Provisional prices may be used. This can replace manually entered prices and periods; review the final price sheet later.
data_description.high_periods: Enter one HH:MM-HH:MM period per line. Times must fall on 15-minute boundaries; overnight periods are allowed.
data_description.low_periods: Enter one HH:MM-HH:MM period per line. Times must fall on 15-minute boundaries; overnight periods are allowed.
data_description.regular_network: Standard gross network price in EUR/kWh. This applies outside the configured high/low periods and outside the selected quarters.
data_description.high_network: Gross high-tariff network price (HT), in EUR/kWh. Enter the network component only, not the full household electricity price.
data_description.low_network: Gross low-tariff network price (NT), in EUR/kWh. Use the same price-sheet year as the standard and high tariffs.
data_description.tariff_year: Year covered by this price sheet. After it expires, cost estimates wait for a valid new-year tariff. Update manually or enable the optional annual refresh.
data_description.active_quarters: Select the quarters in which the operator offers these time-dependent prices. The standard tariff applies during the other quarters. Q1 = Jan–Mar, Q2 = Apr–Jun, Q3 = Jul–Sep, Q4 = Oct–Dec.

cost_module3_prices.description: Review all three gross network prices and their time windows together. Standard tariff applies outside the high/low windows and outside the selected quarters. Use German local time (Europe/Berlin). Source: {source}. ⚠ marks provisional data. Confirm this form to save.

losses.title: Charging losses

menu_options.loss_profile: Use the selected vehicle’s charging history

losses.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Compare energy measured by the wallbox with energy added to the battery during the same completed charge. The last loss and average are estimates. Select the vehicle before charging; missing or ambiguous matches remain unknown instead of reusing another charge.

If no vehicle is selected, choose a profile first. If its charging history is unavailable, check the selected profile under Vehicle profiles or choose an energy sensor.

loss_sensor.title: Charging losses from a sensor
loss_sensor.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Select a sensor reporting the energy added to the vehicle battery during its last charge, in kWh or Wh. Do not select energy measured at the wallbox or a lifetime total. Without charge times, the result is an estimate. By default, confirm the matching charge with the “Assign vehicle charge energy” button.

data_description.charge_loss_auto_match: Optional: assign a changed sensor value received within 30 minutes after unplugging, if this integration observed the complete charge. A changed value cannot prove that both readings belong to the same charge. Leave disabled to confirm each match yourself.
data_description.vehicle_last_charge_energy_entity: Choose battery energy for the last completed charge in kWh or Wh. A charge level in %, the wallbox meter and a lifetime total cannot measure battery charging losses.

loss_vehicle.title: Vehicle charging history
loss_vehicle.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Choose an installed integration with a supported adapter. Generic HA entities can be selected without an adapter. Only existing local vehicle data is read.

loss_vehicle_details.title: Vehicle for charging history
loss_vehicle_details.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Select the vehicle connected to this wallbox. Only existing local charging history is read; no vehicle refresh is requested. Missing or ambiguous matches remain unknown.

options_changed.title: Settings have changed
options_changed.description: These settings or the active vehicle changed while this form was open. Nothing from this form was saved. Continue to reopen the section with the current settings.

cost_network.title: Network price adjustment
cost_network.description: The electricity price has already been selected. Choose no adjustment if it is your final price; otherwise select your agreed network tariff.

data_description.charging_network_module: These options appear when Home Assistant’s country is Germany. Choose the module agreed for this connection. The integration calculates an estimate; it does not apply for a tariff or change your electricity contract.

vehicle_profiles.title: Vehicle profiles
vehicle_profiles.description: Keep each car’s optional data and settings in its own profile. Select the car manually or configure optional automatic selection under Vehicle. Adding a profile does not enable charging features.

vehicle_profile_add.title: Add profile
vehicle_profile_add.description:
Give the profile a recognizable name and choose BavarianData or manual entity selection. New profiles start with optional charging features disabled.

Only installed integrations with a supported vehicle are offered. Manual entity sources always remain available. If a saved vehicle integration is temporarily missing, renaming the profile keeps its existing vehicle and settings.

data_description.vehicle_profile_name: Enter a unique profile name with 1 to 80 characters.
data_description.vehicle_provider: Choose BavarianData only if it is already installed and provides this car in Home Assistant. Manual sources work with other vehicle integrations or helpers; select their entities in each optional feature.

vehicle_profile_edit.title: Edit profile
vehicle_profile_edit.description:
Renaming keeps the settings. Changing the integration or vehicle clears this profile’s feature settings so data from the previous car cannot be reused.

Only installed integrations with a supported vehicle are offered. Manual entity sources always remain available. If a saved vehicle integration is temporarily missing, renaming the profile keeps its existing vehicle and settings.

data_description.vehicle_profile_name: Enter a unique profile name with 1 to 80 characters.
data_description.vehicle_provider: Choose BavarianData only if it is already installed and provides this car in Home Assistant. Manual sources work with other vehicle integrations or helpers; select their entities in each optional feature.

vehicle_profile_select.title: Select vehicle
vehicle_profile_select.description: Select the vehicle connected to this wallbox. Switching clears the previous percentage target and departure plan without starting charging. Each profile keeps its settings and loss average.

data_description.vehicle_profile_id: Select the actual car before starting a charge, especially when comparing charging losses. This manual choice disables automatic vehicle selection.

vehicle_profile_edit_select.title: Edit profile
vehicle_profile_edit_select.description: Choose the profile to edit. Editing another profile does not select that vehicle for charging.

vehicle_profile_remove.title: Remove profile
vehicle_profile_remove.description: Remove the selected profile and its saved feature settings. Removing the active profile also clears its percentage target and departure plan without starting charging.

vehicle_profile_device.title: Vehicle
vehicle_profile_device.description: Select the actual vehicle device in BavarianData. Charge level, charge limit, capacity, departure timers and history can then use this same car; enable each feature separately.

data_description.vehicle_device: Choose the car itself, not the wallbox. Supported data comes from this device only. Unavailable fields are not replaced with data from another car.

vehicle_source.title: Configure charge level
vehicle_source.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Choose the active profile’s reported charge level or select an entity manually. Only the chosen source’s settings follow.

data_description.vehicle_soc_source: The profile source reuses the selected vehicle integration. Manual selection lets you use a different percentage sensor for this profile without changing its other optional data sources.

vehicle_profile_soc.title: Configure charge level
vehicle_profile_soc.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Use the active profile’s reported charge level for the optional percentage target. You can also use that car’s charge limit as an additional maximum. No setting is written to the vehicle.

data.use_vehicle_limit: Also use the vehicle’s charge limit

data_description.use_vehicle_limit: Optional and independent of the charge-level source. A lower vehicle limit reduces the target; a higher limit does not raise it. If this limit becomes unavailable, the last valid value remains in force.

loss_profile.title: Vehicle charging history
loss_profile.description: Use the active profile’s local charging history. No vehicle refresh is requested. Missing or ambiguous matches remain unknown.

vehicle_detection.title: Automatic vehicle selection
vehicle_detection.description: Optional: select the connected car from cable and home signals. Manual selection remains the default. Configure each participating profile, then enable automatic selection.

vehicle_detection_mode.title: Automatic vehicle selection
vehicle_detection_mode.description: Only one car with valid “cable connected” and “at home” signals recently reported to Home Assistant is selected. A definite disconnected or away signal excludes that car. Otherwise, unknown, unavailable or unreported signals for over 30 minutes block selection. If no car or several cars match, no vehicle is selected. Choosing a car manually disables automatic selection. Detection never starts or resumes charging.

data_description.vehicle_auto_selection: If no profile has detection signals yet, the next steps guide you through selecting a profile and its sources. Automatic selection is enabled only after saving valid detection settings. It uses vehicle signals, not identification through the wallbox cable. You can always choose a car manually.

vehicle_detection_profile.title: Configure a profile’s detection signals
vehicle_detection_profile.description: Choose the profile whose cable and home signals you want to configure. Only profiles with detection enabled participate.

vehicle_detection_source.title: Detection signals
vehicle_detection_source.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Use supported local entities from this profile’s vehicle integration, choose existing Home Assistant entities, or disable detection for this profile. Both cable connection and home presence are required. No additional cloud requests are made.

vehicle_detection_entities.title: Cable and home signals
vehicle_detection_entities.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Choose separate signals for this car. Cable connection must be a binary sensor with on = connected. Home presence must be a binary sensor with on = at home, or a person/device tracker with home = at home. Use signals reported to Home Assistant within 30 minutes. Reports do not prove when the car measured its location.

data_description.vehicle_connected_entity: Use this car’s cable-connected signal, not “currently charging”: the car must remain identifiable while paused or fully charged.
data_description.vehicle_home_entity: Prefer the car’s own location signal. A person’s presence is only a useful substitute if it reliably indicates that this car is at home. Two matching cars or uncertain signals prevent automatic selection.

vehicle_plug_charge.title: Virtual Plug & Charge
vehicle_plug_charge.description:
Active vehicle: **{vehicle}**.

Allow this profile to charge automatically here. Activate or deactivate the feature separately with the **Virtual Plug & Charge** switch under **Configuration** on the wallbox device page.

If a profile or its detection signals are missing, use Vehicle profiles below to add or select a car, or Automatic vehicle selection to configure its cable/home signals. Return here afterwards to permit that profile. Automatic profile selection can remain off. A new charging grant needs one uniquely recognized, permitted active profile and a fresh cable report for the current connection. Manual selection alone is not proof of connection.

This optional convenience feature does not use ISO 15118 authentication and requires local RFID authorization to be disabled. Existing pauses, locks and reached targets remain effective. Enabling can stop an ongoing charge while recognition is pending. Disabling does not resume charging; use Charging release explicitly afterwards.

data.vehicle_plug_charge: Allow this vehicle to charge automatically

data_description.vehicle_plug_charge: Permission for the active profile only. Selecting a profile manually is not proof that its car is connected. Fresh matching cable/home signals remain required. Changing the vehicle or its detection sources removes this permission.

error.vehicle_soc_required: Configure a vehicle charge-level source before adding its optional charge limit.
error.invalid_vehicle_entity: Select an entity of the supported type.
error.loss_source_invalid: Select a supported charging loss source and configure its matching vehicle or sensor.
error.cost_source_invalid: Select a supported cost source and a sensor entity for a sensor-based price.
error.cost_price_invalid: Enter a finite gross price in EUR/kWh between −1000 and 1000. Negative prices are allowed.
error.network_tariff_invalid: Check the gross prices, tariff year, two to four active quarters and HT/NT periods. Use one 15-minute-aligned HH:MM-HH:MM period per line; periods must not overlap and must leave standard-tariff time.
error.timed_calendar_required: Choose a calendar for this event title
error.timed_capacity_invalid: Enter a usable capacity between 1 and 250 kWh
error.timed_timezone_invalid: Enter a valid time zone, for example Europe/Berlin
error.options_changed: This section changed while you were editing it. Return and reopen it to use the latest values; your draft was not saved.
error.vehicle_device_invalid: Select a vehicle belonging to the chosen integration.
error.capacity_source_invalid: Select a fixed capacity, a capacity entity or the vehicle profile.
error.tariff_lookup_failed: No unambiguous supported tariff was found. Enter the price-sheet values manually or try importing again later.
error.vehicle_profile_invalid: Select an existing, unambiguous vehicle profile.
error.vehicle_profile_limit: A maximum of eight vehicle profiles can be configured.
error.vehicle_capability_unavailable: The selected vehicle does not provide the required data. Enable the corresponding entity in its integration or choose a manual source.
error.vehicle_profile_name_invalid: Enter a unique profile name with 1 to 80 characters.
error.vehicle_profile_confirm_required: Confirm that you want to remove this profile.
error.vehicle_detection_required: First configure cable and home signals for at least one vehicle profile.
error.vehicle_detection_source_invalid: Select one of the available detection sources.
error.vehicle_detection_entity_invalid: Select an existing cable binary sensor and a supported home-presence entity.
error.vehicle_detection_entities_distinct: Select separate entities for cable connection and home presence.
error.plug_charge_invalid: Choose on or off for this setting.
error.plug_charge_detection_required: Select a vehicle profile and configure its cable/home detection signals before allowing it to charge automatically.

options.8e1: 8E1 - 8 data bits, even parity, 1 stop bit
options.8n2: 8N2 - 8 data bits, no parity, 2 stop bits (default)
options.8o1: 8O1 - 8 data bits, odd parity, 1 stop bit

options.addresses: Search every device address, about 20 seconds
options.full: Search every address, baud rate and frame, several minutes
options.off: Do not search, just report the error

options.none: None; source is the final price

options.profile: Usable capacity from the vehicle profile

set_charging_current.description: Writes the energy-manager charging-current limit of a wallbox. 0 A means no limit, not a charging stop, so it needs the explicit opt-in below.

allow_unlimited.description: Allows writing 0 A, which removes the limit and makes the wallbox signal its maximum current.
allow_unlimited.name: Allow unlimited

current.description: Charging-current limit in ampere. Use 0 A only together with "allow unlimited"; values between 0.01 A and 5.99 A are rejected because the wallbox would signal 0 A.
current.name: Charging current

device_id.description: The wallbox device whose charging-current limit is written.
device_id.name: Wallbox

set_charging_current.name: Set charging current

get_recorder_exclusions.name: Suggest Recorder exclusions
get_recorder_exclusions.description: Return a YAML suggestion using the actual entity IDs. Does not change Recorder or delete history. Merge the list into your existing configuration.

device_id.name: Wallboxes
device_id.description: Wallboxes to include in the suggestion.

profile.name: History profile
profile.description: Keep all history, reduce detail, or keep only energy and power statistics.
